feature: A resized screen repaints its surface
summary: Drag a screen bigger or smaller by a corner and the colour you painted it now fills exactly the new shape. Before this, growing a screen from its bottom-right left the colour at the old size while the outline and everything inside had already moved, so the window disagreed with what got exported.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on: this is how screens draw now.

try.do: Press F and drag out a screen.
Give it a colour with the Fill checkbox in the Color section.
Press V, then drag the screen's bottom-right handle out to make it bigger.
Look along the right edge and the bottom edge of the outline: the colour should reach both.
Drag the same handle back in to make the screen smaller.
Check nothing is left painted outside the outline.
Drag the top-left handle instead, both ways, and check the same two edges.

evaluate: Does the colour keep up with the outline the whole time you are dragging, or only once you let go?
Does resizing a screen still feel as smooth as it did, with no new stutter on a big screen?
If you put something inside the screen and drag it around, does the screen behind it stay steady?
Does a screen with a rounded corner or a border resize just as cleanly?
rough: The screenshots here are real captures of the app, not offscreen renders.
The cost of this is one extra repaint of the screen's own box while you drag its corner. On the 12 megapixel measurement the loop tracks, an edit inside a plain group is still 6.4ms, unchanged.
Only resizing was broken. Moving a screen, or moving something inside it, was always painting correctly, and still takes the cheap path.
